conf.description: entra-id provisioning dataset, api-pull format: Cribl REST Collector against the Log Analytics Query API (AADProvisioningLogs table), column-rename pipeline into logs-azure.provisioning. Unlike the sign-in/audit pulls, SourceIdentity/TargetIdentity/TargetSystem/ProvisioningStatusInfo/etc. are JSON-encoded STRING columns here, not parsed dynamics, so they are JSON.parse'd before their sub-fields are read. This table has no separate activity-time column, so TimeGenerated is converted to epoch seconds and written to _time (Cribl cannot hold a literal '@timestamp' field).

conf.comment: entra-id / provisioning / api-pull: one JS object per row, PascalCase columns; ResultType/ResultSignature/ResultDescription are flat promoted columns read directly, while SourceIdentity, TargetIdentity, TargetSystem, ProvisioningStatusInfo, ServicePrincipal, InitiatedBy, ModifiedProperties and ProvisioningSteps are JSON-encoded STRING columns (not parsed dynamics). Only SourceIdentity/TargetIdentity/TargetSystem are decoded here, gated on identityType===User per the map's explicit instruction (group/SP provisioning shares the same shape); the rest are stored undecoded under their custom targets per the map's own guidance to decode only when needed. Decode expressions call JSON.parse() inline per ternary branch rather than try/catch, since Cribl's eval value is a single expression and also forbids function/arrow declarations (confirmed against this instance). TimeGenerated is written to _time (epoch seconds), not '@timestamp'.

functions.description: document JSON-string-column decode scope, identityType gating, and the single-expression/no-function-scope constraint
rename mapped columns straight to their ECS targets

set _time from TimeGenerated, route unmapped columns to their azure.provisioning.* custom targets, implement the field-table transforms (ResultType outcome normalization, identityType-gated SourceIdentity/TargetIdentity/TargetSystem JSON decode), and tag event.dataset
